question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.160, how long must a Missouri broker retain true copies of business books, accounts (including voided checks), records, contracts, brokerage relationship agreements, closing statements, and correspondence relating to each real estate transaction the broker has handled?
choice_a: At least one year
choice_b: At least five years
choice_c: At least three years
choice_d: At least seven years
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(1) requires every broker to retain true copies of the listed transaction records for a period of at least three years.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.160, retained transaction records must be made available for inspection by the Missouri Real Estate Commission and its authorized agents when?
choice_a: Only after 30 days' written notice from the commission
choice_b: Only during a scheduled annual audit
choice_c: Only if the commission obtains a subpoena
choice_d: At all times during usual business hours at the broker's regular place of business
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(1) requires records to be available for commission inspection at all times during usual business hours at the broker's regular place of business.

question: May a Missouri broker charge a client a separate fee for retaining the transaction records required under 20 CSR 2250-8.160?
choice_a: No, the rule expressly states no broker shall charge a separate fee relating to retention of records
choice_b: Yes, up to $25 per closed file
choice_c: Yes, if the fee is disclosed in the listing agreement
choice_d: Yes, but only for records stored electronically
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(1) states plainly that no broker shall charge a separate fee relating to retention of records.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.160(2), besides retaining property management agreements and related correspondence for three years, what else must a broker retain regarding management activities unless those records are released or transferred?
choice_a: Nothing further beyond the signed agreement itself
choice_b: All business books, accounts, and records relating to the management activities, unless released to the owner(s) or transferred to another broker by a written detailed receipt or transmittal letter agreed to in writing by all parties
choice_c: Only the owner's federal tax filings
choice_d: Only monthly bank statements, with no requirement to retain the agreement
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.160(2) requires the broker to also retain all business books, accounts, and records for management activities unless they are released or transferred as described.

question: Before a Missouri licensee may rent or lease, list for rent, negotiate a lease, or show a property to prospective renters, what must the licensee's broker hold under 20 CSR 2250-8.200?
choice_a: Only a verbal understanding with the property owner
choice_b: A copy of the owner's mortgage payoff statement
choice_c: A current written property management agreement or other written authorization signed by the owner or the owner's authorized agent
choice_d: Only a listing agreement authorizing sale of the property
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.200(1) prohibits property management leasing activity unless the broker holds a current written property management agreement or other written authorization signed by the owner or the owner's authorized agent.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.200(2), may a licensee who is managing the leasing or rental of real estate also act as an agent in the sale or exchange of that same property?
choice_a: No, a property manager may never also act as a sales agent for the same property
choice_b: Yes, with no additional requirement of any kind
choice_c: Only with the Missouri Real Estate Commission's individualized written pre-approval
choice_d: Yes, but only if the licensee complies with the brokerage service agreement requirements of 20 CSR 2250-8.090
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.200(2) permits this dual role provided the licensee complies with the brokerage service agreement requirements of 20 CSR 2250-8.090.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(1), what must a Missouri broker who manages rental property establish and maintain, separate from other trust funds, for the deposit of current rents and money received for property management expenses?
choice_a: A separate escrow account (or accounts) designated as a property management escrow account
choice_b: A single combined escrow account used interchangeably for sales earnest money and rentals
choice_c: A branch-office petty cash fund
choice_d: An interest-bearing personal savings account in the broker's own name
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(1) requires a broker to establish and maintain a separate escrow account designated as a property management escrow account.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(2), where must a Missouri broker maintain security deposits received in connection with property management?
choice_a: Commingled directly with the property management escrow account for administrative convenience
choice_b: Intact, in an escrow account other than the property management escrow account, unless the owner(s) have agreed otherwise in writing
choice_c: In the broker's personal operating account
choice_d: Returned to the tenant automatically within 10 days of receipt
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(2) requires security deposits to be held intact in an escrow account separate from the property management escrow account, pursuant to section 339.105, RSMo, unless the owner(s) agree otherwise in writing.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(3), within how many banking days must a broker deposit money received in connection with property management into the broker's escrow or trust account?
choice_a: Three banking days
choice_b: Thirty banking days
choice_c: Ten banking days
choice_d: Five banking days
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(3) requires deposit within ten banking days of receipt.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(4), what must a property manager (licensee) do with money received in connection with property management?
choice_a: Deposit it directly into the property owner's personal bank account
choice_b: Hold it for up to 10 days before delivering it to the broker
choice_c: Deposit it into the broker's general operating account
choice_d: Immediately deliver it to the supervising broker
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(4) requires a property manager to immediately deliver to the supervising broker all money received in connection with property management.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(5), what type of financial institution must hold a broker's property management escrow account?
choice_a: A bank, savings and loan, or credit union
choice_b: Any licensed title insurance company
choice_c: A bonded third-party property management firm
choice_d: A central depository maintained by the Missouri Real Estate Commission
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(5) specifies the account must be at a bank, savings and loan, or credit union.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6), absent a different written agreement, how often must fees or commissions payable to a broker be withdrawn from a property management escrow account?
choice_a: At least once a week
choice_b: At least once a month
choice_c: Only at the end of each lease term
choice_d: Only annually
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6) requires monthly withdrawal of fees or commissions unless otherwise agreed in writing.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6), rent paid in advance as a deposit for the last month's rent (or as rent other than the current month's rent) held by a broker must generally be deposited into which account?
choice_a: The security deposit escrow account, regardless of any agreement
choice_b: The broker's general operating account
choice_c: The property management escrow account, unless otherwise agreed to in writing
choice_d: An account maintained directly by the Missouri Real Estate Commission
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(6) directs that such advance rent be deposited in the property management escrow account unless otherwise agreed to in writing.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(7), what must a broker execute, upon request of the Missouri Real Estate Commission or its agent, regarding examination of the property management escrow account?
choice_a: A quarterly self-audit certification filed with the county recorder
choice_b: A surety bond application
choice_c: A notarized inventory of managed properties
choice_d: A form entitled "Consent to Examine and Audit Escrow or Trust Account"
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(7) requires the broker to execute the commission's "Consent to Examine and Audit Escrow or Trust Account" form.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.220(8), what must each check, check stub or other disbursement record, and each deposit ticket on a property management escrow account indicate?
choice_a: The related transaction
choice_b: Only the broker's license number
choice_c: Only the date of deposit
choice_d: Nothing beyond the dollar amount
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.220(8) requires each check, disbursement record, and deposit ticket to indicate the related transaction.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.230, disputes over the return of security deposits to lessees are governed by which Missouri statute, in addition to any other applicable law?
choice_a: Section 339.100, RSMo
choice_b: Section 535.300, RSMo
choice_c: Section 339.780, RSMo
choice_d: Section 407.020, RSMo
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.230 states that the return of security deposits to lessees and related disputes are governed by section 535.300, RSMo, and any other applicable law.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9), a written property management agreement between a broker and the property owner must specify which of the following regarding funds?
choice_a: The exact bank routing number of the broker's personal checking account
choice_b: The owner's personal credit score
choice_c: Whether security deposits and prepaid rents will be held by the broker or the owner
choice_d: The broker's total annual commission income from all clients
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(C) requires the property management agreement to specify whether security deposits and prepaid rents will be held by the broker or the owner.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9), besides identifying the managed property and stating the fee or commission terms, what must a written property management agreement contain regarding ending the relationship?
choice_a: A mandatory two-year minimum term with no termination clause permitted
choice_b: Automatic renewal language with no termination option available
choice_c: Only the owner's right to terminate, with no corresponding right for the broker
choice_d: The terms and conditions for termination of the property management agreement by the broker or the owner of the property
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(9)(E) requires the agreement to provide the terms and conditions for termination by either the broker or the owner.

question: Under 20 CSR 2250-8.090(10), once the owner signs a written property management agreement, what must the licensee do, and what must the licensee's broker retain?
choice_a: Give the owner (or the owner's authorized agent) a legible copy of the agreement at the time the owner's signature is obtained, and the broker must retain a copy of the agreement
choice_b: Mail a copy to the owner only if the owner requests it within 30 days
choice_c: File the original agreement directly with the Missouri Real Estate Commission instead of keeping a copy
choice_d: No copy is required unless the agreement is later renewed
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.090(10) requires the licensee to give the owner a legible copy at signing, and requires the licensee's broker to retain a copy of the property management agreement and any signed addendums.

question: Under RSMo 339.105 and 20 CSR 2250-8.120(3), a broker's escrow or trust account (which also holds funds such as security deposits and prepaid rents) must be what type of account?
choice_a: A money market mutual fund
choice_b: A checking account at a bank, savings and loan, or credit union
choice_c: A certificate of deposit
choice_d: A cash-only ledger with no bank account required
explanation: 20 CSR 2250-8.120(3) requires the escrow or trust account maintained under section 339.105, RSMo, to be a checking account in a bank, savings and loan, or credit union.
